Investor brief

A wedding film studio built on one second.

Sekun's Collection is led by cinematographer Cao Vi. It films destination and multicultural weddings for couples whose love story has more than one home, and keeps each one as a numbered film.

Sekun's Collection is a wedding film studio led by a cinematographer. It films the seconds nobody planned, family, ritual and place, for couples whose love story has more than one home, and keeps each wedding as a numbered film in a collection.

See if it fits you

The idea

Sekun is how "second" sounds in his family's accent.

The whole brand comes from that one word. It is the reason the name, the tagline and the logo all say the same thing.

01

A second of film

Film runs at 24 frames a second. The tagline: "Your wedding, at 24 frames a second."

02

The seconds nobody planned

A hand on a shoulder, a parent at the back of the room. These are what the films are built around.

03

Where he comes from

The name keeps the accent. The brand is at home between cultures because its founder is.

The opening

Most wedding films compete on price. A few are booked on taste.

Sekun is built for the second group, and for a kind of couple the market serves poorly.

The couple

More than one home

Two cultures, two ceremonies, a wedding abroad or a trip home to marry. They want family and heritage filmed with respect, not as a novelty.

The gap

Loud or generic

The usual choice is a highlight reel cut to trending audio, or a luxury studio that looks like every other one.

The position

A cinematographer, not a videographer

Sekun is compared on its eye, so it is chosen like a photographer or a designer, not like a line on a budget.

Why it wins

Four things, hard to copy together.

Any studio can claim one of these. Sekun's edge is all four at once.

The eye

Cao Vi is trained as a cinematographer. He films the edges of the room: family, hands, ritual and place. Storytelling is the promise, and it does not depend on any trend.

Fluent between cultures

He grew up between two cultures. A tea ceremony, a bow or a speech in a second language is filmed plainly and up close, by someone who understands what it means.

One signature look

Natural light, muted warm color and visible grain, often on Super 8 and 16mm. Couples book the look, so there is no menu of styles to dilute it.

A collection, not a catalogue

Each wedding becomes a numbered film with its own label, such as "No. 047 · Da Nang". A service turns into something kept, and every film sells the next one.

What already exists

The brand is built. It is ready to be used.

Strategy, identity and voice are finished and documented, so new money goes into growth, not into figuring out what Sekun is.

Growth

Three ways couples find Sekun.

Partners

Photographers and planners

They already serve these couples and need a filmmaker who matches their taste. Each shared wedding gives them a clip to post.

Search

Being found by name and place

Every film is tagged by city and country, so a couple searching for a wedding film in Da Nang or Los Angeles can find one.

The archive

Every film sells the next

Numbered films build a visible body of work. The longer the collection, the stronger the case.

The plan

What investment builds

Money goes into proof and reach.

These are the five places capital would go. Amounts are not set yet.

01

Destination portfolio

Filming selected weddings abroad to fill the collection with the work the brand is known for.

02

Film and cameras

Super 8 and 16mm stock, developing, scanning and equipment, so real film can be offered on every commission.

03

A second cinematographer

One more person trained in the Sekun look, so the studio is not limited to one calendar.

04

Website and brochure

A home for the collection, with open starting prices and a film page for each numbered wedding.

05

Partner program

Time and travel to build relationships with planners and photographers in Los Angeles, Orlando and abroad.

The ask is open. The amount, the terms and the business figures are for a direct conversation with Cao Vi. This page is here to show what you would be backing.

Is it you

Probably not a fit

  • You want fast scale through volume and discounts.
  • You would ask Sekun to follow trends, add styles or shorten the films into content.
  • You see a wedding film as a commodity.

Founder

Cao Vi, cinematographer.

The first thing I ever wanted to understand was a shot. A bonfire, close up, and one person far down the beach. I was a kid in front of the television, wondering how the focus moved from the fire to the person.

After that, an old Nikon came on every family trip. In middle school I took my uncle's camera, without asking, to film a cultural festival. He spent the whole day reporting it stolen and searching the neighborhood.

I'm still that kid. The more I film, the more the seconds matter to me.

Based in Los Angeles and Orlando, filming worldwide.

What is still being built

  • The studio rests on one person's eye today. A second cinematographer is part of the plan.
  • The audience is small and the relaunch is just starting.
  • Past weddings are being numbered and published as the collection.

Wherever your story takes place.
